title: Derived closed-fibre restriction for proper schemes over henselian pairs
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $f:Y\to X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-proper-morphism], and put $Y_0=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ with its projection $i:Y_0\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $K\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}})$ have torsion abelian cohomology sheaves, with the derived category and torsion convention of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The canonical restriction morphism is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$:
$$\rho_{Y,K}:R\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{et}},K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma((Y_0)_{\mathrm{et}},i^{-1}K).$$
Here inverse image on abelian sheaves is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], $R\Gamma$ means total right derived global sections computed by bounded-below injective resolutions [def-sp-kinjective-bridge], and the arrow is the derived cohomological pullback induced by the adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. The isomorphisms are natural in $K$. More generally, if $(A,I)\to(B,J)$ is a morphism of henselian pairs, $g:V\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is proper, $h:V\to Y$ is compatible with the base morphism, $L\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}})$ has torsion cohomology, and $h^{-1}K\to L$ is specified, then the square of the two restriction morphisms $\rho_{Y,K},\rho_{V,L}$ with the induced cohomological pullbacks is commutative. Finite generation of $I$, Noetherianity, excellence, and invertibility of torsion primes are not assumed.

source.place: Tags 09ZI (theorem-gabber), 0DDE (lemma-proper-base-change), 0DDD (lemma-torsion-direct-image); derived proper henselian-pair restriction obtained by applying these to the proper structural morphism and canonical truncations.

proof.text: For any scheme map u, identify canonical restriction with the derived unit followed by the Leray comparison. Use the shift-compatible exact right-derived base-change transformation, whose source is derived sections followed by the exact derivation of the identity. The canonical identity comparison identifies its components with the canonical restrictions and preserves invertibility. Both functors are triangulated and preserve every lower cohomology bound. Apply the bounded-below heart test to the desired restriction along the closed-fibre projection i. It suffices to prove invertibility on F[0] for each torsion cohomology sheaf F of K.

Fix a torsion abelian sheaf F on Y. Properness gives that f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the standard scheme morphism instances. Put E=Rf_*F[0]. For n>=0, apply the qcqs higher-image torsion theorem with the set of all primes to H^n(E); use the geometric-stalk characterization to obtain local torsion. For n<0, the lower bound zero of F[0] gives H^n(E)=0, which is torsion. This avoids proving preservation of torsion for arbitrary derived complexes and avoids the general truncation spectral sequence.

source.place: Tag 0DDD (lemma-torsion-direct-image), applied to a sheaf rather than a complex.

proof.text: For every torsion abelian sheaf G on Spec A, use the equivalence with sheaves of ULift Z-modules and apply Gabber comparison. The derived-global/Ext pullback comparison identifies each nonnegative homology map of canonical restriction on G[0] with the classical cohomology map under additive equivalences. It is therefore invertible. Both source and target have zero negative homology. Cohomology detects isomorphisms in D+, so restriction on G[0] is an isomorphism. Apply the bounded-below heart test to E, whose cohomology is torsion by the preceding step, to prove that restriction along z:Spec(A/I)->Spec A is invertible on E.
Proper base change gives the canonical isomorphism beta:z^-1 E -> Rf0_*i^-1 F[0]. Thus restriction along z on E, followed by derived sections of beta and the Leray comparison for f0, is invertible.

Prove composition of canonical restriction directly from the bounded-below derived adjunction unit composition law and associativity of the right-derived composition isomorphisms. The ordinary direct-image/terminal-section comparisons associate because the maps to the terminal object agree. Derive this equation to obtain associativity of Leray. Naturality of Leray, followed by the derived unit composition law, then proves restriction composition. Exact derivation respects composition and inverse of natural isomorphisms by its localization characterization, so the recorded square compositor is the inverse of one diagonal compositor followed by the other. It follows that restriction respects every commutative square.

source.place: Tag 015M; cohomology.tex Tag 01F8. The private helpers give the localization and adjunction calculation in Lean.

proof.text: Expand beta into its derived adjunction unit, square inverse-image comparison and pulled-back counit. Move the two coefficient maps past Leray by naturality, use the restriction square from the preceding step, and move the counit past restriction by naturality. The triangle identity then contracts restriction along f followed by derived sections of its counit to the Leray map for f. Hence the invertible composite of step 4 is Leray_f followed by canonical restriction along i. Cancel the invertible Leray factor. This proves the sheaf case F[0], and the first heart test gives the assertion for K.

source.place: Tag 07A7; derived.tex Tag 015M, the adjunction triangle identity and the mate calculation.

proof.text: Naturality in K is the naturality equation of the right-derived descent defining the canonical pullback. For a morphism of henselian pairs, the quotient ring map and the fibre-product projection identity give the commutative square with its canonical fibre map. Apply restriction composition along its two diagonals and naturality along the specified coefficient morphism a. The square compositor is exactly abelianDerivedSquareInverseImageIso, so the resulting coefficient map is exactly abelianDerivedSquareCoefficientMap. Neither properness nor torsion is needed for this equality; those hypotheses give invertibility of its restriction sides.

proof_origin.place: W6: Tags 09ZI, 0DDD and 0DDE, using two applications of the existing bounded-below heart test. Only higher images of degree-zero torsion sheaves are needed. The canonical-map and square equalities use the bounded-below derived adjunction and Leray composition APIs directly.

lean.note: The three theorem declarations state invertibility, naturality in K, and naturality for arbitrary compatible maps of henselian pairs with a specified derived coefficient map. The three auxiliary definitions construct the canonical fibre map and coefficient identification from quotient maps, fibre products and exact derived inverse-image compositors. D+(Ab) is the full bounded-below subcategory of D(Ab), so its IsIso and square equality are exactly the asserted ambient derived statements.
